pr_title: roachtest: backup-restore/mixed-version use system db when querying job status
pr_body:
Previously in `waitForJobSuccess()` in the backup-restore/mixed-version test, if the job was a full cluster restore that dropped `defaultdb`, the query to the jobs table would fail with `pq: database "defaultdb" is offline: restoring` as our connection was to `defaultdb`, which is dropped during full cluster restore. We fix this by adding an option to connect to a different database in roachtests and connecting to the system database in `waitForJobSuccess()` instead.

Fixes #110165

Release note: None
pr_comments: This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/cockroachdb/cockroach/110208)

I'm wondering if this change is worth the trouble. If the restore eventually succeeds, the connection should work just fine after the `defaultdb` is available again. IMO, we should improve the error reporting instead to indicate that the test timedout waiting for the restore to finish.

I think like this approach.

There ultimately is no fundamental guarantee that `defaultdb` exists; it is a db we happen to make when we create a new cluster, but it can be dropped (and is dropped by RESTORE, then replaced assuming the restored backup includes it).

If a given test specifically wants to test for the existence of defaultdb, then sure, fine, it should do that, but if all we're trying to do is get an open sql connection to use to inspect a job or other system status attribute, I see no reason to couple that to defaultdb existing, and it seems clearer to instead use a db that it is assured will always exist, which means system.
Fair points. If we're touching the test in this PR, maybe we could also improve the error reporting to include something like "timed out while waiting for job to finish"?

>  maybe we could also improve the error reporting to include something like "timed out while waiting for job to finish"?

I changed the error to be a different message `exhausted all %d retries waiting for job %d to finish` if we've used up all retries.

My guess here is that this is a problem in the test runner. Namely, we drop the defaultdb at the beginning of a full cluster restore, so we can't use a conn that is going to try to connect to defaultdb to run status checks.

We can maybe fix it by connecting to the system database instead.

> connecting to the system database instead.

discussed in meeting today, this is our plan.

> We can maybe fix it by connecting to the system database instead.

This will fix the status checking, but the underlying error is that the test timed out waiting for the restore to finish (we could improve the error message here). As you can see, the job is still running after ~1h20mins.

Maybe this is #108676 again (just a guess as it's another timeout on a 22.2 restore).
